answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable membership bond before it can submit proposals, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm a fraudulent claim. The bond does not prove a person is unique, but it makes a swarm of disposable identities expensive: an attacker must tie up real capital for every account and risks losing it. At a summit, cedar-backed attestations might help reviewers compare claims; at the nadir, the bond still imposes a cost even if those attestations fail.
